text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000112 bills 99215 at roughly double the all-provider rate in every complexity band, but with no documented 99215 claims the records cannot yet show whether this is upcoding or an unusually acute panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The panel is genuinely complex, with 5+ condition patients the largest band, and most 99215s fall on multi-morbid patients such as C0062101 and C0062292. Still, the 99215 share runs about two times the all-provider share within every condition band, including 0-1 conditions, so complexity alone does not explain the excess. Combined with heavy 99214 use, that points to a uniform shift toward higher codes, which is consistent with upcoding but could also reflect acuity the condition count misses. The sampled low-complexity 99215s are the clearest concern: C0062089 (age 22, no chronic conditions, back pain), and C0063125 and C0063236 (same patient, an upper respiratory infection and a Z09 follow-up) are hard to square with high-complexity medical decision making. Documentation is too thin to judge: only six charts came back, none of them for 99215 claims. A reviewer should first request records for the 99215 claims, starting with the low-complexity examples above, and compare documented MDM and time against the billed level."}
